messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — I ran KV cache paging experiments across A100/us-west1 and H100/eu-west1 for the new lx-ggml-quant bring-up. Short summary + raw charts in S3: s3://redwood-bench/kv/1715551234. Need feedback on eviction policy tuning before we bake into runtime.

trevor: Nice. Can you paste p50/p95 and hit-rate numbers here? Especially by sequence bins (32 / 256 / 2048).

maya: TL;DR — paging=ON, eviction=LRU, page_size=256KB, per-GPU cache ~6GB. Results (A100 / us-west1):
- short (32): p50 12ms, p95 28ms, hit 98%, throughput ~60k toks/s
- med (256): p50 22ms, p95 120ms, hit 86%, throughput ~24k toks/s
- long (2048): p50 140ms, p95 520ms, hit 34%, throughput ~4.2k toks/s

jin: 34% hit on long is concerning. What's the page_size and eviction threshold?

maya: page_size 256KB, eviction threshold 85% of cache. We tried LFU too — LFU bumped long hit to ~38% but increased churn on med, raising p95 there by ~10-12%.

sara: Suggest trying 128KB page_size and eviction threshold 80% to reduce large-page fragmentation. Also which kernel selector was used?

maya: Kernel selector: fused_attention_v2 on A100, attention_split on H100 (autotune via runtime v0.9.2). Command I ran:

```
bench_kv --model lx-ggml-q4_0 --batch 1 --seq_bins 32,256,2048 --kv_paging on --page_size 256k --evict_policy lru --gpu A100 --region us-west1 --out s3://redwood-bench/kv/1715551234
```

infra-bot: Build 2024.11.3 deployed to us-west1 (runtime v0.9.2) — experiments reproducible.

trevor: For capacity sizing — what's the mapping from tokens/s to GPUs for the med workload?

maya: Med (256) numbers are tokens/s per GPU. A single A100 delivered ~24k toks/s under paging=ON. So for target 100k toks/s you'd need ~5 GPUs (plus headroom for spikes).

ops-team: How did H100 compare in region?

maya: H100/eu-west1: lower p95 on long (p95 ~420ms vs 520ms on A100), higher long throughput (~6.8k toks/s) — likely due to larger L2 and kernel efficiency. Hit% broadly similar across GPUs.

jin: Eviction policy nuance: LFU helps long sequences since repeated prefixes re-hit, LRU favors short interactive patterns. Maybe a hybrid (freq-weighted LRU) would work better.

sara: Quantization note: using q4_nomap reduced KV memory footprint and increased hit-rate by ~3% vs q8, but decode latency per-token slightly worse. Tradeoffs to consider.

trevor: Can someone drop the latency vs hit-rate charts as small PNGs in this thread? S3 link alone is hard for PMs.

maya: Uploading now: https://bench.redwood.ai/kv/1715551234/latency_vs_hit_short.png, https://bench.redwood.ai/kv/1715551234/latency_vs_hit_med.png, https://bench.redwood.ai/kv/1715551234/latency_vs_hit_long.png

infra-bot: Upload complete: latency_vs_hit_short.png, latency_vs_hit_med.png, latency_vs_hit_long.png

ops-team: Plan suggestion — run a matrix next week: page_size 128k & 256k, eviction_threshold 80% & 85%, eviction_policy LRU/LFU/hybrid, on both A100 and H100. Also test kernel toggle fused_attention_v2 vs attention_split.

maya: Agreed. I'll prepare the bench matrix + k8s job template. Also FYI enabling background prefetch (prefetch_threads=2) reduced med p95 by ~15% in our runs.

jin: Add a synthetic customer distribution (70% short, 25% med, 5% long) to the matrix — we need hit-rate-weighted latency estimates for capacity planning.

sara: I'll add Datadog instrumentation: cache_hit, cache_evictions_per_sec, page_faults_per_sec, avg_eviction_size.

trevor: Can we aim to ship a default of page_size=128k + eviction_policy=hybrid in runtime RFC by end of sprint?

maya: Yep — I'll open an RFC, attach raw traces and the perf matrix. Thanks all :rocket: 

ops-team: :thumbsup:

jin: :+1:
